mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate at 0.14% (below 0.5%) indicates an accommodative monetary policy that reduces equity discount rates, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days. This relationship holds as long as the rate remains at the zero bound.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of instances where FEDFUNDS is below 0.5%, or the Rank IC for FEDFUNDS < 0.5% is below 0.03 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate falls below 0.5%, it signals an aggressive monetary easing cycle that boosts equity valuations, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of instances where FEDFUNDS < 0.5%, or the Rank IC for FEDFUNDS < 0.5% is below 0.03 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of high unemployment (UNRATE > 8%) and low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS < 0.5%) indicates a recessionary labor market with accommodative monetary policy, which typically precedes positive equity returns over the next 20 trading days.
regime_hint: recessionary labor market with monetary accommodation
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of instances where UNRATE > 8% and FEDFUNDS < 0.5%, or the Rank IC for the interaction condition is below 0.03 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) exceeds 225, it indicates a high-inflation regime that triggers central bank tightening, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances where CPIAUCSL > 225, or the Rank IC for CPIAUCSL > 225 is below 0.03 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) falls below 95, it signals a contraction in manufacturing output, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as the economy enters a slowdown phase.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances where INDPRO < 95, or the Rank IC for INDPRO < 95 is below 0.03 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Low housing starts (HOUST < 500) indicate weak consumer demand and residential investment, which typically results in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days as the market prices in economic weakness.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances where HOUST < 500, or the Rank IC for HOUST < 500 is below 0.03 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A joint condition of low housing starts (HOUST < 500) and low industrial production (INDPRO < 95) indicates a broad-based economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances where HOUST < 500 and INDPRO < 95, or the Rank IC for the interaction condition is below 0.03 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: High unemployment (UNRATE > 8%) signals a weak labor market that often precedes equity market corrections, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances where UNRATE > 8%, or the Rank IC for UNRATE > 8% is below 0.03 over a 3-year rolling window.
